episode_summary: November 2017 episode on the collapse of the SegWit2x fork, the Bitcoin Cash split and Litecoin competition, with an interview with J.R. Willett about Coin.me's crypto ATM network and the UpToken token sale, plus the Parity multisig freeze.

cards.claim: In November 2017 the SegWit2x fork was called off after many backers signed an agreement to drop it for lack of consensus.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: So a good portion of the people that were backing it signed something that basically said, we're not going to do this. We're calling the fork off.

cards.claim: In November 2017 the host argued that many people were still chasing free coins from the 2x fork, as they had with Bitcoin Cash.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: I feel like there's still a good portion of people that want to take advantage of people's ignorance and get their money somehow or some other way.

cards.claim: In November 2017 the hosts warned that large holders could pump a forked coin and then sell, leaving buyers with a worthless coin.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: you can you know make people buy it because they think it's going to be worth something and then if you hold a significant amount you just sell it off

cards.claim: In November 2017 the host predicted that whichever Bitcoin chain offered better utility, Bitcoin Cash or SegWit Bitcoin, would become the real Bitcoin.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: whoever is going to end up providing the better user experience or enterprise experience or whoever ends up providing a better utility for the network will end up becoming

cards.claim: In November 2017 the host said Bitcoin's price rise was unhealthy because people were hoarding it rather than using it.
cards.speaker: unknown
cards.quote: But I don't feel like the reason for the price rise is good. It's not a healthy reason for the price rise. It's people just hoarding.

cards.claim: In November 2017 the hosts noted that Ethereum produced blocks about every 14 seconds.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: blocks every 14 seconds and you have ether coming into the system every 14 seconds

cards.claim: In November 2017 the host said people sent money on Ethereum faster and more cheaply than on Bitcoin.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: And people send money using Ethereum faster than Bitcoin. At a rate faster than Bitcoin. At a rate cheaper than Bitcoin.

cards.claim: In November 2017 the host said an Ether transaction he sent just after DEVCON took half an hour to confirm.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: it took a half an hour for that thing to get confirmed

cards.claim: In November 2017 the host said there were about three million traditional ATMs and only about a thousand crypto ATMs.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: there's three million traditional ATMs, and there's only like a thousand crypto ATMs

cards.claim: J.R. Willett said Bitcoin was trading at 25 cents when he first started learning about it in 2010.
cards.speaker: J.R. Willett
cards.quote: 2010 was when I first started learning about Bitcoin and Bitcoin at the time at that time was 25 cents.

cards.claim: J.R. Willett said in 2011 he disguised Bitcoin mining software and paid people from Craigslist to run it on their video cards.
cards.speaker: J.R. Willett
cards.quote: I actually I took the Bitcoin mining software and I wrote a wrapper around it to disguise it. And I got random people on Craigslist who had video cards to run it.

cards.claim: J.R. Willett said the first initial coin offering, for the token then called Mastercoin, took in about half a million dollars of Bitcoin over about 30 days.
cards.speaker: J.R. Willett
cards.quote: And random people over the course of about 30 days sent me half a million dollars worth of Bitcoin.

cards.claim: J.R. Willett said the token from the first ICO, later renamed Omni, rose about a hundredfold after its offering.
cards.speaker: J.R. Willett
cards.quote: omni went from uh the the initial offering it went up a hundredfold

cards.claim: J.R. Willett said Omni was still operating and hosted about half a billion dollars of assets.
cards.speaker: J.R. Willett
cards.quote: Omni is still going today, by the way, it hosts, uh, half a billion dollars worth of assets.

cards.claim: J.R. Willett said he preferred to be the one selling shovels in a gold rush rather than digging for gold.
cards.speaker: J.R. Willett
cards.quote: if there's a gold rush on, I like to be the guy selling shovels, not the guy digging.

cards.claim: J.R. Willett said Coin.me's ATMs charged fees ranging between 5 and 10 percent.
cards.speaker: J.R. Willett
cards.quote: I think that CoinMe's ATMs range between 5% and 10%, for instance.

cards.claim: J.R. Willett said Coin.me's founders reported that each of its ATMs averaged about a hundred thousand dollars a month.
cards.speaker: J.R. Willett
cards.quote: The each ATM on average does a hundred thousand dollars a month.

cards.claim: In November 2017 the host said Coin.me operated about 40 ATMs while most ATM operators had only two or three.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: A lot of them have just two or three. Coin.me has 40.

cards.claim: J.R. Willett said pre-sales to wealthy insiders at discounts bothered him in token sales.
cards.speaker: J.R. Willett
cards.quote: one of the things that bothers me is the what you might call the pre-sale

cards.claim: J.R. Willett said UpToken reserved about 25 percent for the company, locked until 500 ATMs were deployed.
cards.speaker: J.R. Willett
cards.quote: And we did reserve, I think, 25% for the company's future use. However, it's locked.

cards.claim: J.R. Willett said he put over a million dollars into the UpToken sale as soon as it started.
cards.speaker: J.R. Willett
cards.quote: So yeah, I put over a million dollars into the token sale as soon as it started.

cards.claim: J.R. Willett predicted that one coin would someday be worth a trillion dollars, though he did not know which one.
cards.speaker: J.R. Willett
cards.quote: I think we're going to someday have a trillion dollar coin I don't know which one it's going to be

cards.claim: J.R. Willett said he hoped the developing world would skip building banking infrastructure and move straight to crypto portals.
cards.speaker: J.R. Willett
cards.quote: And I'm hoping that the developing world will skip building a giant banking infrastructure

cards.claim: J.R. Willett predicted the general public would not self-custody crypto and would instead rely on trusted third parties to hold it.
cards.speaker: J.R. Willett
cards.quote: But I think that the general public is not going to make that leap.

cards.claim: J.R. Willett said Coin.me would buy UpToken worth 1 percent of its ATM transactions and give it to customers as cash back.
cards.speaker: J.R. Willett
cards.quote: CoinMe is continually, forever, going to be purchasing Uptoken to the tune of 1% of their ATM transactions.

cards.claim: J.R. Willett said UpToken holders would get 30 percent off Coin.me ATM fees paid in UP tokens.
cards.speaker: J.R. Willett
cards.quote: So they get 30% off of all their ATM fees that are paid with UP token.

cards.claim: J.R. Willett said the only reason to use blockchain is when some government stands in the way of what you want to do.
cards.speaker: J.R. Willett
cards.quote: the only reason to use blockchain is if some government somewhere is in the way of what you want to do

cards.claim: In November 2017 the hosts said the Parity multisig wallet bug locked and froze about 300 million dollars worth of Ether in smart contracts.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: which locked up and froze about 300 million dollars worth of ether in these smart contracts

cards.claim: In November 2017 the host explained that someone called an unprotected function in the Parity library contract, which killed the library and froze the wallets that depended on it.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: somebody basically called a function that they should not have access to

cards.claim: In November 2017 the host expected Bitcoin Cash holders receiving Coinbase's January 1 release to possibly dump it and crash the price.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: that January 1st when Coinbase releases those Bitcoin cash to their customers

title: TBP166 - ATMs and ICOs
